transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-12-22
Time: 08:00 PT / 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Amir Castillo (Redwood CSM), Carlos Mejia (CTO, HelioGrid), Nora Patel (Head Infra), Samir Gupta (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, brief):
HelioGrid is evaluating Redwood for inference hosting for robotics telemetry and model-in-the-loop control. Primary concerns: SOC2 and ISO posture, customer-managed KMS, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC and audit logging, data retention for telemetry, and private VPC/on-prem options. Next steps include sending SOC2 artifacts, networking diagram, and scheduling a deeper technical deployment call.

Topics:
- Compliance posture (SOC2, ISO)
- Authentication and IdP (SSO/SAML, SCIM)
- Encryption key management (KMS, BYOK, HSM)
- RBAC, tenant isolation and audit logs
- Data retention, deletion, and telemetry handling
- Deployment model tradeoffs: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)

Action items (short):
- Redwood to share SOC2 report and KMS integration doc
- HelioGrid to send VPC/net diagram and list of compliance controls
- Schedule technical deep dive for private deployment networking

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for taking time. We're Jordan from Redwood, joined by Priya, our solution engineer, and Amir who runs customer success. How's the calendar look?
[00:09] Carlos Mejia: Morning — thanks. Quick note, we're doing a security-first evaluation, so most of the time will go to questions about controls, encryption, and hosting options.
[00:17] Priya Nair: Totally understood. We'll focus on SOC2, ISO, SSO, KMS, RBAC and logging — and then map those to Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private options.
[00:25] Nora Patel: Great. We're especially interested in KMS and whether the key material stays in our control. Also need clarity on audit log retention — for us it's 7 years for some telemetry.
[00:35] Jordan Lee: OK, on KMS we support customer-managed keys for Private and Dedicated, and for Hosted we have a BYOK flow via your cloud KMS — there are details but yes you can bring keys.
[00:45] Samir Gupta: Sorry to interrupt — BYOK meaning we bring a key into Redwood? We need assurance the key isn't exported, and HSM-backed is required for a couple of our workflows.
[00:53] Priya Nair: Short answer: HSM-backed KMS is supported. For Private deployments the control plane can be customer-managed; keys never leave your KMS. For Hosted, we do an envelope encryption with your master key — Redwood doesn't keep plaintext keys. (slight pause) There's a doc we can share that diagrams the key flow.
[01:10] Carlos Mejia: Can you follow up with that? We'll need specifics for our security team.
[01:15] Jordan Lee: Absolutely — Priya will upload the KMS integration guide and the SOC2 Type II report.
[01:20] Priya Nair: Noted. Also want to call out our encryption-at-rest and in-transit defaults — TLS1.2+, AES-256 for disk. Some of the auto-transcription may call it AES two fifty, you'll see variations.
[01:33] Nora Patel: On SSO, we use Okta and need SAML + SCIM for provisioning. Does Redwood support SCIM for user sync?
[01:41] Priya Nair: Yes — SAML SSO with SAML 2.0 and SCIM provisioning is supported across all deployment modes. For Dedicated and Private you can restrict IdP endpoints in the VPC. There are RBAC primitives too — roles, groups, and token scoping.
[01:55] Samir Gupta: How granular is RBAC? We need separation between infra engineers and product engineers and also SREs. And we want immutable audit logs for admin actions.
[02:04] Priya Nair: We support role-based roles — apologies, role-based access control with pre-defined roles and custom roles. Audit logs are write-once in our system and we can export to your SIEM (syslog, S3 or Splunk). Exports can be push or pull and we can set retention policies.
[02:18] Carlos Mejia: Exporting to our SIEM is non-negotiable. Can logs include request-level metadata (API keys, user ids, model id, route)?
[02:25] Priya Nair: Yes, we capture token-level request metadata, call latency, model version, route, and anonymized user ids by default — though PII fields are redacted unless you opt-in to include them for troubleshooting under an NDA. Small caveat: some telemetry like KV cache hits are best-effort in Hosted due to shared infrastructure, but Dedicated/Private gives full fidelity.
[02:45] Nora Patel: About data retention — we want to ensure model input data (telemetry) is deleted within 30 days and that any logs older than 7 years are purged per policy. How does Redwood handle deletion and configurable retention?
[02:56] Jordan Lee: We offer configurable retention windows per tenant and per data class — e.g., inference payloads, embeddings, logs. For Hosted there are default retention tiers and we can do retention at 30/90/365 days. For Dedicated and Private you control the retention in the deployed storage and we provide helper APIs to purge.
[03:15] Samir Gupta: Are deletions synchronous? We need cryptographic deletion proofs for certain data sets.
[03:21] Priya Nair: For Private deployments, you can use KMS key rotations+destroy (cryptographic delete) and Redwood can surface an audit event for the deletion. For Hosted we provide deletion APIs and a deletion workflow, and we can provide attestation logs — we'll need to follow up to map to your compliance evidence needs.
[03:37] Carlos Mejia: Good. Now about certifications — do you have SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001?
[03:43] Jordan Lee: We have SOC2 Type II; ISO 27001 is in progress this quarter. We'll share the SOC2 report, plus our InfoSec policy pack.
[03:50] Nora Patel: Any third-party pen test results?
[03:53] Amir Castillo: We run annual third-party pentests and will share redacted reports when appropriate. We'll also share a summary of open/closed findings and remediation timelines.
[04:02] Samir Gupta: Networking — if we go Private, we expect a private control plane in our VPC or air-gapped. Can you outline what outbound connections Redwood components expect?
[04:11] Priya Nair: For Private there are two flavors: (1) Private control plane with customer-managed networking where no public ingress is required — everything sits inside your VPC, we deploy a connector, and egress is minimized; (2) On-prem package for air-gapped where we ship the runtime and you can run it isolated. For Dedicated you'll have a managed VPC peering and limited outbound to our artifact repo for updates unless you set up a mirror. We'll send a port/IP list.
[04:41] Carlos Mejia: We need the exact CIDR and egress ports so our firewall folks can review.
[04:45] Jordan Lee: We'll include a network checklist; Samir, you're the security owner — we'll get that to you.
[04:50] Samir Gupta: Yup. Also curious about multi-tenancy: do you multitenant on Hosted? How is isolation enforced between customers?
[04:58] Priya Nair: Hosted is multi-tenant but with strong logical isolation: cryptographic separation of keys, token scoping, and container-level isolation. Dedicated gives you tenant-isolated GPU pools, and Private is fully single-tenant. If you need hardware-level separation we recommend Dedicated or Private.
[05:15] Nora Patel: Latency concerns for robotics loops — will Dedicated give us the determinism we need?
[05:22] Priya Nair: Yes, Dedicated provides reserved GPU capacity, pre-warmed instances and predictable batching profiles. For the most deterministic use cases we recommend Private deployed in your region or on-prem.
[05:33] Carlos Mejia: Anything else on compliance: data residency for EU? We're global and need EU-only residency for some customers.
[05:40] Jordan Lee: We have regional hosting and can lock workloads to EU regions for both Hosted (with region selection) and Dedicated/Private. We'll pull our data residency guide.
[05:48] Samir Gupta: How locked down is the console? Admin console access — can we restrict IP ranges?
[05:54] Priya Nair: Yes, for Dedicated and Private you can lock console access behind your SSO and enforce IP allowlists. Hosted supports session policies and IP allowlist at org level. There's also MFA enforced org-wide.
[06:06] Carlos Mejia: Regarding change management, do you provide release notes and can we schedule maintenance windows?
[06:12] Amir Castillo: Yes — scheduled maintenance windows are configurable for Dedicated/Private. Hosted gets scheduled windows but we provide advance notice; for Dedicated we coordinate with your infra team. Release notes and CVEs are posted to our portal.
[06:24] Nora Patel: Backups — how are backups encrypted and where are they stored?
[06:28] Priya Nair: Backups are encrypted with AES-256 and use your KMS for key wrapping in Dedicated/Private. For Hosted, backups are encrypted and keys are envelope-wrapped with your master key if you BYOK. Storage locations follow region residency.
[06:42] Carlos Mejia: We want an SLA for response times on security incidents and a runbook for incident handling.
[06:48] Jordan Lee: We have incident response SLAs for Dedicated customers (sec tiered in contract). We'll share an IR runbook and pager escalation matrix.
[06:56] Samir Gupta: Is there a SOC hotline or security contact?
[07:00] Amir Castillo: Yes, we provide a security contact and an on-call rotation for customers with a support contract.
[07:05] Nora Patel: A few smaller but important items: data classification tags on requests, ability to redact sensitive fields before forwarding to a third-party model, and support for labeled retention policies per project.
[07:16] Priya Nair: We have request-level metadata tagging and a transform hook that can redact fields before persistence. For Hosted we have safe defaults; Dedicated/Private give you full control over transforms.
[07:30] Carlos Mejia: For the pilot we want to run 3 models, one small local model and two larger variants. We'll probably start on Hosted to move fast but want a path to Dedicated if latency and isolation needs increase. What's a typical pilot length?
[07:43] Jordan Lee: Typical pilots are 4–6 weeks. We'll propose a pilot SOW in the follow-up that outlines success criteria, telemetry dashboards, and a scope for the three models.
[07:52] Samir Gupta: Onboarding access — can we get a demo tenant with SAML so we can test provisioning?
[07:58] Priya Nair: Yes, we can provision a demo tenant with Okta SAML and SCIM. We'll make sure audit log forwarding is enabled so you can validate exports.
[08:08] Carlos Mejia: One last question on retention proofing: if we request deletion and you claim data is purged, do you provide an audit log or proof artifact?
[08:16] Priya Nair: We can produce an audit event and a deletion attestation for Private and Dedicated. For Hosted we provide deletion logs and can coordinate a joint attestation process under NDA. We'll need to align on the format of the proof with your compliance team.
[08:30] Jordan Lee: Ok, let's recap next steps — we'll (1) share SOC2 Type II and pentest summary, (2) send KMS BYOK flow and key diagram, (3) provide network checklist and IP/ports, (4) propose pilot SOW and schedule a SE deep dive the week of Jan 5.
[08:45] Carlos Mejia: That works. Samir and Nora — anything to add?
[08:49] Samir Gupta: Just that we'll send our VPC diagram and list of compliance controls.
[08:53] Nora Patel: And we'll need price ranges for Hosted vs Dedicated to feed procurement.
[08:59] Jordan Lee: Jordan will email the pricing ranges and the team will follow up.
[09:03] Amir Castillo: I'll set up the deep dive invite and add the SE runbook review.
[09:07] Carlos Mejia: Thanks everyone.
[09:09] Jordan Lee: Thanks — we'll follow up by Friday with the artifacts.

(End of recording)
